title: Pruning & Knowledge Distillation
interviewAnswer: Pruning removes low-value parameters or structure; distillation trains a smaller student to mimic a larger teacher. Both can reduce serving cost, but structured pruning usually maps to hardware better than arbitrary sparsity, and distillation quality depends on the teacher targets and task.
why: Parameter count is not the same as real latency. Compression methods matter only if the runtime can exploit them.
intuition: Pruning asks “what can I remove?” Distillation asks “can a smaller model learn the useful behavior of the bigger one?”
deepDive: Unstructured sparsity may compress well yet remain slow on dense kernels. Distillation can use logits, intermediate representations or generated data. Always benchmark final hardware and evaluate task-specific regressions.
workedExample: Distill a 1B classifier into a 100M student using teacher probabilities, then compare latency and calibration—not just top-1 accuracy.
commonMistakes: Distilling only on easy examples and losing rare behavior.
followUps: When is pruning preferable to quantization?
production: Compression belongs in a cost/quality optimization loop with deployment benchmarks and rollback criteria.
